about:
Setup

Stellar Blade demo, frame 59: Eve leaving the escape pod (full frame). Output 4K, FSR Quality (render 2561x1441). DLSS 5 neural rendering (small model) before upscaling, then 4.1.2l-lossy (FSR 4.1.2 Lite, our build). RX 7800 XT, Linux/Proton.

What to look at

As found leaves dark trails behind the flying particles and dark spots on Eve; ours removes nearly all of them (pixels more than 25 levels darker than an every-frame run: 2,949 vs 80 on this frame). Ours also spreads the network over all four frames instead of one long frame every 4th frame.

What got worse

Ours is slightly brighter than the every-frame reference over a wider area, so by overall dB as found measures slightly closer (frame 59: 37.54 vs 36.88 dB; frames 1-62: 40.43 vs 39.03 dB): ours carries an older edit on part of each frame.

Rough max attainable fps on this GPU

Fps you can hold with every frame on time (no stutter), rough estimate: 1.8x
As found≈ 36 fps
Ours≈ 64 fps
Average fps is about the same (as found ≈ 64, ours ≈ 66): both do the same work, ours spreads it over every frame instead of one long frame in four.
Frame time, ms, four frames in a row (estimate; line = 16.7 ms, 60 fps):
As found28121212
Ours15151615

Estimates for the setting played in the game (4K output, 1920x1080 render). Ours was measured there holding the 60 fps cap, with neural rendering at 4.2 ms per frame on average and 4.7 ms at most. The game's own frame time was not measured (assumed about 11 ms). As found: the whole network (about 17 ms at that size, estimated from measured sizes) on one frame in four, about 0.5 ms on the others. Average = from the mean frame time. Smooth = from the slowest frame type: the fps you can hold if every frame must be on time.

Notes

Frames from a captured game clip; display mapping is ours (x/(1+x), gamma 1/2.2), not the game's tone mapping; no UI or post-processing. DLSS 5 network run via the community AMD port (mauri870/DLSSNR-RDNA3); not affiliated with NVIDIA. Pictures: this project's local test harness, one run each (deterministic).
